key_insight: Simulations show that a 24-arm fractal vane produces nearly axisymmetric yielding, while improved conversion expressions support more accurate rheological measurements.
engineering_relevance: Better vane designs and torque-to-stress and rotation-to-strain-rate conversions can improve characterization of yield-stress materials.
method: Model viscoplastic flow using the Herschel–Bulkley constitutive law.
Use augmented Lagrangian finite elements in 2D and regularised finite volumes in 3D.
Compare 4-arm, 6-arm and 24-arm fractal vanes and revisit circular Couette conversion assumptions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive 2D and 3D simulations across a broad parameter range, but provides no quantitative error reductions or experimental validation details.
watch_item: This is a numerical rheometry study, not an AI surrogate; conversion accuracy should be checked for the intended geometry and material parameters.
paper_title: Three-dimensional computational rheometry of viscoplastic fluids in vane-in-cup fixtures
